output.title: Mathematical understanding of a shortcut connection
output.caption: A residual-style block where the input from Layer 1 goes through a function F and is also added directly via a shortcut, producing f(x_l)+x_l; below it, derivative expressions indicate the gradient includes an added 1 term.
output.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  A["Layer 1"] --> B["F"]
  A -->|"shortcut"| C["+"]
  B -->|"f(x_l)"| C
  C --> D["f(x_l) + x_l"]
  D --> E["L"]

claims.text: The input from Layer 1 is sent into a function block F.
claims.reason: The diagram shows an input from layer 1 (x_l) entering a block labeled F.

claims.text: The input from Layer 1 also bypasses F through a shortcut path.
claims.reason: A bypass arrow routes x_l around F directly to the addition node.

claims.text: The shortcut path and the output of F are added together.
claims.reason: The output of F and the shortcut path meet at a plus/addition point.

claims.text: The result after addition is labeled f(x_l) + x_l.
claims.reason: The post-addition output is annotated as f(x_l) + x_l (written near the output of the add block).

claims.text: The combined output f(x_l) + x_l feeds into L.
claims.reason: An arrow from the summed output points to L, indicating it feeds into L.

claims.text: The diagram expresses a shortcut connection from an earlier layer to a later point after F.
claims.reason: The structure explicitly depicts a residual/shortcut connection from the earlier layer input to a later point after F (the add node).

claims.text: The derivative notes indicate that when differentiating through the residual connection, an added 1 term appears.
claims.reason: The derivative working shows terms like ∂f(x_l)/∂x_l + 1, indicating the added 1 from the shortcut when differentiating.

claims.text: The gradient with respect to the earlier layer includes both the derivative through f(x_l) and the direct shortcut contribution.
claims.reason: The gradient expression includes both the path through f(x_l) (a derivative term) and the direct shortcut contribution (+1 term), matching residual backprop.
